comment: Ids reserved for records in preparation - assigned but not yet published. Reserved ids are permanent: they will publish when verified, and are never reused for anything else. Neutral by design; no record content lives here. Distinct from retired ids (rejected candidates, CVE convention), listed under `retired`: an id that was assigned to a candidate in a public pull request and then rejected before registration. Retired ids never publish and are never reused; the entry names the date, the rejection reason and the public discussion.

retired.reason: Candidate rejected before registration. The draft recorded a claim, made by LiteLLM during incident response, that a coding agent had written developers' GitHub CLI OAuth tokens into gateway logs behind the litellm 1.107.0 release compromise of 2026-10-21. LiteLLM's canonical 2026-10-23 attack-chain post withdrew that explanation (the first token came from an internal agent-platform API reached with a master key committed to a public repository); the revised account establishes no agent action as the credential-exposure vector (it does not say who originally inserted the exposed key), so the event is out of scope.

Candidate rejected before registration: activity against UNCTAD's statistics API reconstructed by swarmcha.se and attributed to OpenAI from payload tags; not acknowledged by OpenAI, task instructions unknown, no exceeded usage terms found, so agent divergence was not established. Possible overlap with PIR-2026-0094.

Candidate rejected before registration: a population-level account of unauthorised agents in US bank customer accounts, resting on anonymous executives relayed through Axios; no individual incident or institutional attestation of an agent exceeding its customer's instructions.

Candidate rejected before registration: a composite of an estimated monitoring-coverage gap, auditor-found possible exploits and deliberately tasked red-team agents (METR, Redwood Research, OpenAI); intended capability testing, with no agent diverging from its legitimate operator.

Draft closed before registration: a researcher's report that ChatGPT's GitHub connector made unrequested cross-repository writes; the sole write-up was replaced by an embargo notice and the write-capable product surface was unresolved.
Draft closed before registration: a founder's self-report that a Grok Bot agent posted his bank data to a company Slack channel; single-party, unverified, and disputed by a reported Community Note.
